title: Can LLMs Debug Robots by Editing Their Weights?
read_level: partial (full main text and discussion; appendices skimmed via search only)
why_wsp: GPT-6 Astra reads robot policy weights in a CPU Python workspace and writes replacement tensors (65 token-embedding rows of pi0.5), guided by budgeted simulator rollouts, with gradient updates forbidden.
domain: robot manipulation foundation policies (VLA pi0.5, FastWAM) on LIBERO variants, simulation
target: openpi pi05_libero (3.62B parameters exported); FastWAM; edits also attempted on LIBERO-Plus/PRO/RECOVER settings
self_editing: no; external LLM edits robot policy
fraction_or_count_of_weights_changed: "It changes 132,768 scalar entries across 65 rows, or 0.00367% of the exported checkpoint." (Sec 3.3)

headline_results.claim: Best session improves held-out paraphrase success 86.3% to 92.0%
headline_results.quote: the best raises success from 86.3% to 92.0% (48 repairs, four regressions; exact paired p = 1.31 x 10^-10)
Three independent sessions on pi0.5 all improve success on 765 held-out paraphrases
Among the 335 instructions containing edited tokens, success rises from 74.3% to 87.5%; the other 430 episodes have zero outcome changes.

headline_results.claim: Random-direction control does not help; full replacement explains much of the gain
headline_results.quote: Full replacement using the editor's own lexicon explains much of the gain but produces more regressions; its direct difference from the editor is not significant at 0.05.
Across 13 further robot sessions, the editor declines 12 candidates; the sole retained edit does not show a significant held-out gain.
FastWAM succeeds on 147 episodes with task-only instructions and 102 with tagged instructions: 70.0% versus 48.6%

headline_results.claim: Reproduced Takehi et al. Qwen3.5-0.8B edit
headline_results.quote: With one sample per MATH-500 problem, it scores 49.4%, compared with the report's 48.1% using four samples.

cost.quote: Robot sessions receive 40-50 requests; all three language-repair sessions receive 50. A Python execution may use up to 900 seconds and 96 GB of CPU memory.
complete API cost accounting is not available.

baselines_and_controls: unedited policy (paired McNemar), random-direction edit of same 65 rows with matched norm (one realization), full destination replacement using editor's own lexicon, norm-only vs direction-only replay controls; LoRA, prompt rewriting, human lexicon explicitly not measured
runs_and_variance: 3 independent pi0.5 sessions (one held-out seed 7); 16 sessions total; exact McNemar with Holm correction; practice validation across 5 rollout seeds shows seed 73 negative. Quote: "Independent sessions test whether the editor can find an edit again; shared variants and one held-out seed limit claims about environmental generalization."
robustness_of_edits: Seed sensitivity on practice validation (Table 5, seed 73 loses 2 net successes); structural locality guarantee for instructions not containing edited tokens; no fine-tuning/quantization tests; simulation only
verification: statistical (exact paired McNemar tests, Holm correction); structural locality argument; tensor-hash checks
memorization_vs_reasoning: Editor-informed dictionary control shows lexical correspondence explains much of the gain; random-direction control rules out edit-size effects. Editor diagnosed a gripper-flip correlate as a consequence rather than cause in recovery sessions.
limitations_stated: Edits narrow and lexical; no retained confirmed repair for visual, recovery or task-change failures; not compared to human lexicon, prompt rewriting or LoRA; simulation only, two checkpoints; one held-out seed; editor consumes observations so not data-free; no full API cost.
code_or_data: reproducibility package described; "Public code and weight-hosting links will be supplied with the artifact release." (none found)
notes_for_survey: Applies tool-assisted, simulator-feedback WSP to a 3.6B VLA; the repair is an embedding-row lexical remapping, with an editor-informed full-replacement control not significantly worse. Records 12/13 declined candidates in other failure categories, framing the obstacle-vs-ability distinction as a hypothesis.
